scheme_name: National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG)
overview: The National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG) is a Government of India initiative aimed at improving logistics efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing competitiveness of Indian goods in domestic and international markets. It focuses on integrated development of the logistics sector through policy interventions, infrastructure development, technology adoption, and skill development. The policy aims to create a seamless, technology-driven, and integrated logistics ecosystem across the country.
objectives: Reduce logistics cost from 14% to less than 10% of GDP by 2025
Improve India's ranking in Logistics Performance Index to top 25 by 2030
Create a technology-driven integrated logistics ecosystem
Develop multimodal logistics infrastructure including multimodal logistics parks
Promote adoption of technology in logistics including automation, IoT, AI, and blockchain
Develop skilled manpower for the logistics sector
Promote sustainability and green logistics practices
Enhance competitiveness of Indian goods in global markets
eligibility: The policy applies to all stakeholders in the logistics ecosystem including logistics service providers, infrastructure developers, technology providers, manufacturers, traders, e-commerce companies, agri-logistics entities, and startups operating in the logistics sector across India. There are no specific eligibility restrictions as it is a policy framework rather than a beneficiary-specific scheme.
benefits: The policy provides a framework for integrated development of the logistics sector including: development of multimodal logistics parks, implementation of a Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) for seamless data exchange, standardization of logistics processes, skill development and capacity building in logistics, promotion of green logistics, improvement of first and last mile connectivity, reduction in logistics costs and time, enhancement of cargo safety and security, and creation of a conducive policy environment for logistics innovation and investment.
financial_support: The National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG) is a policy framework and does not provide direct financial support to entities. Financial support for logistics infrastructure and initiatives is provided through various central and state government schemes, public-private partnerships, and institutional financing. The policy enables convergence of existing schemes and facilitates access to funding through various government programs.
application_process: As a policy framework, the National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG) does not have a specific application process for beneficiaries. Implementation occurs through various government schemes, programs, and initiatives aligned with the policy objectives. Stakeholders can benefit by participating in relevant government schemes, applying for logistics infrastructure projects, adopting ULIP, and engaging in skill development programs under the policy framework.
deadlines: As a policy framework, the National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG) does not have specific application deadlines. Implementation timelines vary for different schemes and initiatives aligned with the policy objectives.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
caveats: The National Logistics Policy – Ease of Logistics (ELOG) is a policy framework and does not provide direct financial benefits or subsidies
Benefits are derived through participation in aligned government schemes and initiatives
Implementation depends on coordination between central ministries, state governments, and private sector stakeholders
Policy effectiveness depends on timely implementation of complementary schemes and infrastructure projects
